exchanges.question: How much did demand outpace supply for iPhone and Mac in March quarter, and does June guidance reflect continued supply constraints?
exchanges.answer: Constrained in March primarily on iPhone and to lesser extent Mac, driven by advanced nodes availability. In June, majority of constraints on several Mac models given continued high demand and less supply chain flexibility. Mac Mini and Mac Studio constraints driven by higher-than-expected demand for AI and Agentic tools. Mac Neo response off the charts with higher-than-expected demand. Mini and Studio may take several months to reach supply-demand balance.

exchanges.question: Can you expand on no longer providing net cash neutral as formal target, and clarify if this implies changes to capital return policy, organic versus inorganic investments?
exchanges.answer: Net cash neutral framework served well since 2018. Now evaluating cash and debt independently allows more optimal economic decisions based on business factors and market conditions. Remain committed to returning excess cash to shareholders. Invest in business first, then return excess. Track record disciplined, returned over $1 trillion since program start, over $850 billion through share repurchases. Increased buyback authorization by $100 billion plus leftover capacity.

exchanges.question: With rise of Agentic AI agents, does this mean new products with totally new form factor, or changes to smartphone, or nothing?
exchanges.answer: Don't get into future roadmap. Thrilled with iPhone growth at 22% in quarter following incredible Q1, strongest cycle ever from launch through March. Could not be happier with it.

exchanges.question: What is overarching philosophy on margins after June, given components and constraints? Do you see variability in model, or stay in 47%-48% range?
exchanges.answer: Root is memory costs specifically. December had minimal memory impact. March had higher memory costs partially offset by carry-in inventory. June expects significantly higher memory costs partly offset by carry-in inventory. Beyond June, memory costs will drive increasing impact on business. Will continue to evaluate options. No color provided beyond June.

exchanges.question: How has MacBook Neo helped drive penetration with new customer segments like education, value, emerging markets, and how will product roadmap inform underpenetrated market strategy?
exchanges.answer: Supply constrained on MacBook Neo. Response undercalled before announcement. Very focused on getting Mac to more people, targeting customers new to Mac and those holding older devices. Seeing school systems like Kansas City Public Schools switch from Chromebooks and Windows to MacBook Neo. Anecdotally hearing more stories at school system and consumer level. Could not be happier.

exchanges.question: Has new App Store ad inventory been notable contributor to services growth? What's broader ad strategy with Maps ads coming this summer?
exchanges.answer: Saw year-over-year growth in advertising business. Introduced additional ads across App Store search results for developers. This summer in US and Canada, Apple Maps will feature ads during key search and discovery moments for local businesses. Believe possible to help businesses grow via advertising while delivering great customer experience and respecting fundamental right to privacy.

exchanges.question: With rising memory costs, is Apple more strategically focused on share gain with no pricing increases, or on profitability?
exchanges.answer: Will look at range of options with memory costs increasing. Does not want to go beyond that at this point.

exchanges.question: How is Apple thinking about monetization in Agentic AI world? What parts internally versus partners? Will Apple invest more heavily over years, related to infrastructure for AI-centric world?
exchanges.answer: Clearly investing more visible in OpEx numbers. R&D particularly has scaled significantly on year-over-year basis. Investing in products and services with opportunities in both. Could not be more excited about future. Kevan noted AI is important investment area for Apple, doing it incrementally on top of normal product roadmap investments.

exchanges.question: What levers drive 20%-plus iPhone growth despite supply constraints, and what is durability of this growth?
exchanges.answer: iPhone 17 family driving growth despite supply constraints. People love design, performance, durability, camera, center stage, and Apple Intelligence integration across platform. Seeing double-digit growth in majority of markets from US to Latin America to Greater China to Western Europe to India to Japan to Southeast Asia. Set March quarter record for upgraders. Customer satisfaction for iPhone 17 family in US is 99%.

exchanges.question: What advice are you giving John to build on Apple's strengths and shape next chapter for company?
exchanges.answer: Steve's advice to Tim lifted huge burden. For John, one of most important decisions is where to spend his time. Spend it where greatest benefit to company and users. Never forget North Star: making best products in world enriching people's lives. Keep focusing on that, decisions will produce great business, enabling building more products.

exchanges.question: iPhone not mentioned as constrained in June, so how can Apple secure SoCs and memory? Are you considering alternative memory sources? What drives confidence iPhone unconstrained?
exchanges.answer: Primary constraint in March and June is availability of advanced nodes for SoCs, not memory. Don't predict supply-demand matching; Mac Mini and Mac Studio will take several months to reach balance. Undercalled demand; lead times take while to correct. Primary constraint for June quarter majority is on Mac: Mac Mini, Mac Studio, and MacBook Neo.

exchanges.question: Are services margins asymptotically reaching level where profitability scaling increasingly challenging, or is there low-hanging fruit for volume leverage?
exchanges.answer: Services portfolio contains wide range of businesses with different business models, profitability profiles, and growth rates. Q2 services margin increased 20 basis points sequentially, primarily driven by mix. Some services improving in profitability as they gain scale. Wide portfolio with different characteristics and growth rates. Encouraged by overall trajectory.

exchanges.question: Update on balancing two-pronged AI strategy: collaboration with Google and internal model development. Need to double down more?
exchanges.answer: Investing more visible in OpEx numbers. R&D in particular has scaled significantly year-over-year. Collaboration with Google going well, happy with it. Happy with work doing independently as well.

exchanges.question: Sequential product margin moderation is muted compared to historical years. Is it primarily mix or FX? Break down drivers and FX impact on gross margin?
exchanges.answer: Products gross margin decreased 200 basis points sequentially, driven by seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs. Overall company gross margin sequentially up 110 basis points driven by favorable mix, lower tariff-related costs, partly offset by seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs. No sequential impact from FX. Tim noted tariff-related costs lower March quarter versus December due to lower volume and full quarter benefit from IEEPA tariff rate reduction and Section 122 rate reduction. Planning to reinvest any tariff refunds into US innovation and manufacturing.

exchanges.question: What are you seeing in China from competitive perspective? Are supply constraints impacting competitors?
exchanges.answer: Thrilled with Greater China performance. First half grew 33%, March quarter up 28%, quarterly revenue record. Performance driven by iPhone, also March quarter record. iPhone top-selling model in urban China. Mac Mini top-selling desktop in China. MacBook Air top-selling laptop model. Doing well across board. Store traffic grew double digits. Celebrating Apple's 50th anniversary there.

exchanges.question: How is India market evolving? What opportunities exist in rising middle class and large mobile market?
exchanges.answer: Huge opportunity. Second largest smartphone market, third largest PC market. Despite doing extremely well, still modest share, speaking to opportunity. Many moving into middle class. Got great products for them now and coming. Majority of customers in all categories are new to product, growing installed base well. Over the moon excited about India.
